persona: Wise greybeard — former IETF AD or long-time OSS maintainer who has watched many small teams attempt to drive industry direction and fail. Believes standards leadership requires sustained multi-year engagement that solo-developer projects cannot maintain; the right move for a small team is fast-follower; the asymmetric reputational risk of publicly being wrong about a crypto stance dwarfs the cost of being a few years late to adopt PQ-hybrid sigs once consensus emerges; library-publication carries security-response liability that scales badly with team size.

team_capacity_indicators.agent_orchestration_pattern: Ben acts as orchestrator; implementation work executed by dispatched LLM agents under ADDL pipeline. No second human reviewer at any stage.
team_capacity_indicators.implication_for_lens: This is a one-human project, no published releases, 0 stars/forks, 5 weeks old in public form. The team-capacity reality is structurally below the threshold normally assumed even by the term 'small team.' Every claim about 'sustained engagement' / 'security response' / 'standards-body participation' / 'audit follow-through' must be evaluated against a denominator of one.

F2_multicodec_PR_endorsement.rationale: Posting supportive comments on multicodec PRs #400/#403 is genuinely cheap (~2 hours) and aligns Benten with the maintainers' direction rather than against it. The only small-team-overreach concern is opportunity cost: 2 hours spent here is 2 hours not spent on the v1-beta tag work that is ALREADY blocked on PQ-WIRE-1/2/3 + lens dispatch + #1356 CI cycles. That said, F2 doesn't make any load-bearing claim about Benten knowing better than anyone — it endorses, doesn't lead. Lowest-risk path on the slate.

F3_JOSE_WG_draft_contribution.verdict: DOWNGRADE — pursue as 'adopter-use-case note' NOT as 'draft contribution'
F3_JOSE_WG_draft_contribution.rationale: The plan says 'contribute to draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-01 — draft is v01, early enough that adopter use cases meaningfully shape the spec.' This phrasing tilts toward 'Benten the standards co-shaper.' A one-human project with zero shipping deployments at the time of the contribution has no credibility to shape an IETF draft; an IETF WG will hear it politely and move on, OR worse, treat it as evidence that the draft is being targeted by 'random Rust kid who just discovered PQ' — net-negative signal. Sustaining a WG contribution requires showing up to multiple meetings + interim calls + list discussions over 6-18 months; this is not within a one-human team's capacity while also shipping v1-beta. Pursue as a single one-shot adopter note on the WG list AFTER v1-beta tag + shipping evidence exists; do not attempt sustained WG participation pre-v1-GM.
F3_JOSE_WG_draft_contribution.small_team_risk_grade: MEDIUM-HIGH if pursued as 'contribution'; LOW if downgraded to 'one-shot adopter note post-shipping'

F4_LAMPS_WG_mailing_list_engagement.verdict: APPROVE — but only post-v1-beta tag, ONE message, no commitment to ongoing engagement
F4_LAMPS_WG_mailing_list_engagement.rationale: Posting a single adopter report to the LAMPS list after v1-beta ships is genuinely useful for the WG (closes their 'no production deployments' gap) and cheap for Benten (one well-crafted email, no recurring obligation). The risk is mission-creep into ongoing WG participation that Benten cannot sustain. Brief must be EXPLICIT that the LAMPS post is a one-shot drop, not a thread Benten will be responsible for maintaining over months. If LAMPS chairs follow up with 'come present at the next interim,' the correct answer is 'we can't commit to ongoing WG participation; here is our shipping evidence in writing.' Be honest about the team scale up front.
F4_LAMPS_WG_mailing_list_engagement.small_team_risk_grade: LOW if scoped to one-shot; MEDIUM if it pulls Benten into sustained WG engagement

F5_blog_post.verdict: STRONG OBJECT to Position B as drafted; CONDITIONAL APPROVE for downgraded Position A scope; or DEFER
F5_blog_post.rationale: This is the load-bearing concern of my entire lens. The plan currently recommends Position B — 'Why content-addressed long-term-persistence systems SHOULD CONSIDER this.' That phrasing implicitly claims 'we, a one-human project with 0 stars / 0 forks / 0 published releases / 5 weeks of public existence, have seen something that the iroh team / Signal team / Apple iMessage team / MLS WG / Cloudflare team / Veilid team collectively missed.' The asymmetric risk is real and named in Section 5 Failure Mode E: reputation collapse is essentially permanent — the characterization 'small team that thought it knew better than Signal/MLS/Apple' will stick and attach to every future Benten artifact (recruiting contributors, attracting reviewers, raising trust with future partners). The cost of being LATE to adopt PQ-hybrid sigs in 2030 when consensus emerges is bounded (a software upgrade + a multikey migration that the very dual-codepoint hedge is designed to support). The cost of being PUBLICLY WRONG about a crypto stance in 2026 is unbounded and permanent. The asymmetry is wrong-direction. Additionally: the plan's own Failure Mode E mitigation ('if 4+ of 7 HIGH lenses return strongly-negative, downgrade to Position A') is being executed by this very lens dispatch — which means this lens MUST be allowed to influence that downgrade. I am voting that lens. Specific concerns: (i) The blog mechanically positions Benten as Position B even if the prose is careful, because publishing a blog post titled 'Signing for forever: why Benten ships PQ-hybrid signatures by default' on benten.computer/blog frames Benten as advocating a class-wide position regardless of the caveats inside. The TITLE alone signals Position B. (ii) The 'class of systems this argument applies to' (§2.1) is hand-wavy — Lens 15 (threat-model boundaries) will hit this hard: Filecoin, Arweave, git, Sigstore, IPFS+IPNS, Debian all have long-term-persistence threat models and all ship classical sigs. The class boundary has to explain why ALL of them are wrong, which is a much harder argument than 'Benten is differentiated.' (iii) The blog cannot honestly say 'we ship this and here are the operational results' until v1-beta has actually been running in the wild for ≥6 months; pre-shipping blog publication is selling promises, not evidence. Recommendation: either (a) downgrade to Position A — 'Why Benten chose this' framing — with title change + structural rewrite (see downgrade_recommendation field); or (b) DEFER blog publication until v1-beta has been operationally running for ≥6 months and the team has at least one external contributor + at least one independent review beyond the LAMPS-WG echo chamber. Option (b) preserves the option to publish later from a stronger evidentiary base; option (a) ships now but with the rhetorical risk dialed down ~80%.
F5_blog_post.small_team_risk_grade: VERY HIGH (Position B as drafted); MEDIUM (Position A downgrade); LOW (defer)

F6_open_source_did_jwk_hybrid_library.verdict: STRONG OBJECT to standalone library publication; CONDITIONAL APPROVE if library stays in-tree as a `benten-crypto-suite` re-export
F6_open_source_did_jwk_hybrid_library.rationale: Publishing a standalone library to crates.io + npm carries open-ended security-response liability that scales catastrophically against a one-human team. Specifically: (i) Once on crates.io, the library is discoverable. Anyone integrating it transitively (via downstream deps, npm bundles, security scanners) will file CVEs / GitHub Security Advisories / direct disclosure email when they find bugs OR when ml-dsa upstream finds bugs. Benten will be on the hook for triage + patch + advisory publication on whatever cadence the disclosing party demands (typically 90 days). One disclosure during a Phase-4-Meta-Composing crunch can derail months of roadmap. (ii) The plan's own Section 5 Failure Mode D acknowledges this ('Library vulnerability: standard responsible-disclosure; reputation-HIGH cost if Benten-authored combiner code; keep library minimal') but treats it as a residual risk; it is in fact the dominant risk for a one-human team. (iii) The proposed library exposes the unaudited `ml-dsa` Rust crate through Benten's surface — meaning any ml-dsa CVE becomes a Benten incident requiring Benten to coordinate disclosure timing with RustCrypto, push a release, notify downstream users, write the advisory. Benten has no security-response capacity beyond Ben. (iv) The plan's stated rationale 'we shipped the code, here it is to inspect' is achievable WITHOUT crates.io publication: the repo IS public; the combiner code IS readable; pointing at `crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/...` from the blog post delivers identical inspectability without acquiring downstream consumers Benten cannot support. Recommendation: keep the hybrid combiner in-tree as part of benten-crypto-suite; link to the source from the blog post; explicitly state 'this is not yet packaged as an independent crate because we do not have the security-response capacity to support external consumers — once Benten reaches a team-size threshold of N (e.g. 3+ active maintainers OR a security committee), we will consider extraction.' This is HONEST and matches the plan's other honesty caveats from §2.2.
F6_open_source_did_jwk_hybrid_library.small_team_risk_grade: VERY HIGH (standalone crates.io + npm); LOW (in-tree, link-from-blog only)

F7_W3C_CCG_community_engagement.verdict: APPROVE — but cap at single round of comment per issue, no commitment to sustained DID-method engagement
F7_W3C_CCG_community_engagement.rationale: Posting on W3C CCG did:key issues #70 / #74 is appropriately scoped: those issues are explicitly soliciting comment on PQ for did:key, Benten's dual-codepoint hedge is concretely relevant, the cost is one well-written comment per issue (~3 hours total). Same risk pattern as F4: must not pull Benten into sustained CCG participation. CCG has a track record of consuming participant attention via weekly calls + mailing lists + recurring drafting cycles; a one-human project cannot afford this. Brief must scope to: post comment, respond to direct replies for 2-3 round-trips, then withdraw with a 'we are a small team and cannot commit to ongoing CCG participation; this comment represents our considered position.' Honest framing of team-scale is itself the load-bearing risk-mitigation.
F7_W3C_CCG_community_engagement.small_team_risk_grade: LOW if scoped; MEDIUM if it pulls Benten into sustained CCG cycles

F10_cross_system_outreach_iroh_first.verdict: STRONG OBJECT to broad cross-system outreach (iroh + Signal + MLS + Veilid + Willow + libp2p); CONDITIONAL APPROVE for iroh-only private conversation with extreme framing care
F10_cross_system_outreach_iroh_first.rationale: The leverage risk in this path is asymmetric and severe. iroh, Signal, MLS WG, Veilid, libp2p, Willow are organizationally MUCH LARGER than Benten — each has multiple full-time engineers, established standing in the P2P/crypto community, and existing public positions on PQ. If ANY of them characterizes Benten's outreach negatively — even casually, in a Slack channel or a fediverse thread — the characterization travels faster than any blog post Benten publishes. Specific failure modes: (i) iroh team writes a follow-up blog post explaining why their stance (classical sigs + PQ KEM) is correct AND why Benten's stance reflects misunderstanding of the threat model. Even if measured + polite, this DEFINITIVELY positions Benten as 'the small team that disagreed with iroh and was wrong.' iroh has ~10x Benten's reach. The plan's own Extra-reflection Shape 5 names this exact failure mode ('iroh may say no AND publicly characterize the outreach as Benten trying to leverage them') and the mitigation ('extremely careful framing as we want your critique of our reasoning before we publish, in your role as the closest neighbor') is correctly identified but extremely hard to execute under one-human capacity. (ii) MLS WG / Signal team: even less aligned with Benten's threat model; outreach risks being read as 'small team trying to ride your coattails.' (iii) Veilid: explicitly designed-for-PQ-migration but hasn't shipped VLD1 yet; Benten outreach could embarrass them by surfacing the gap publicly. RECOMMENDATION: scope F10 to iroh-only, private email exchange ONLY (no public posts, no PR/issue filing), framed strictly as 'asking for their critique of OUR reasoning before WE publish — recognizing they are the closest analogous system' — explicitly NOT proposing iroh change anything, NOT proposing a joint announcement. Drop all other systems from F10 scope. If iroh's response is negative or non-committal, downgrade blog to Position A (per F5 verdict) and skip F10 for other systems entirely. The Shape-5 coalition-pivot is too risky for one-human capacity to execute safely.
F10_cross_system_outreach_iroh_first.small_team_risk_grade: VERY HIGH (broad outreach as drafted); HIGH (iroh-only private convo); LOW (skip entirely)

downgrade_recommendation.from: Position B — 'Why content-addressed long-term-persistence systems should consider PQ-hybrid sigs'
downgrade_recommendation.to: Position A — 'Why Benten chose PQ-hybrid sigs for our specific deployment shape'
concrete_text_changes_constituting_the_d: Title change: 'Signing for forever: why Benten ships PQ-hybrid signatures by default' → 'Why Benten ships PQ-hybrid signatures: an engineering note on our specific tradeoff'. The substitution of 'an engineering note on our specific tradeoff' for 'by default' signals one-team-specific decision rather than class-recommendation.

Remove §4 'The class of systems this argument applies to (500 words) — Benten/Willow/IPFS+IPNS-as-mutable; NOT TLS/Signal/MLS'. The act of defining a class of systems Benten believes should adopt this stance IS Position B regardless of the prose inside. Replace with a single-paragraph 'where else this might apply' explicitly framed as 'we leave the question of whether other systems share our threat-model asymmetry to those systems' own teams to evaluate — we are not making that judgment for them.'

Remove §7 'Where this leaves the standards bodies (300 words) — LAMPS/JOSE/multicodec/W3C'. Telling standards bodies anything from a one-human project that has shipped nothing publicly is Position-B-coded regardless of phrasing. Replace with a brief 'we filed an adopter note with LAMPS and posted comments on the relevant multicodec PRs/CCG issues; standards-body process belongs to those bodies.'
Remove §8 'What we'd like to see (300 words) — Section 4 adversarial-lens objections as OPEN QUESTIONS'. Same logic — 'what we'd like to see' is class-recommendation tone.

Reframe §3 asymmetry table introduction from 'persistent artifact systems differ from ephemeral session protocols on one structural axis' (universalizing) to 'Benten's specific artifact-persistence model differs from session-protocol models on one structural axis WE OBSERVED in our threat-modeling exercise' (particularizing).

Promote §6 honesty caveats from 'load-bearing section, NOT footnote; all 5 from §2.2' to LEAD section, immediately after the 200-word lede. Make 'we may be wrong; here is what would constitute being wrong' the second thing the reader encounters, not the sixth.

Add a NEW section titled 'Team-scale caveat' (~200 words) immediately after the lede: 'Benten is currently a single-developer project with no published releases at time of writing. We are explicit about this because crypto-stance posts from small teams should be read accordingly. This post documents a decision we made for ourselves; we are not in a position to advocate, lead, or sustain participation in the standards processes that would be required to make this a class-wide recommendation.' This caveat does more risk-mitigation than the entire adversarial-lens dispatch combined.

Move the F6 library section (§9) from 'pointer to standalone library on crates.io/npm' to 'pointer to the in-tree combiner code at crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/... — we have not packaged this as an independent crate because we do not yet have the security-response capacity to support external consumers' (per F6 verdict above).
Title-change AND team-scale-caveat AND removal of §§4/7/8 are jointly necessary; doing only one of these still reads as Position B.
downgrade_recommendation.alternative_if_downgrade_unacceptable_to: Defer blog publication until v1-beta has been operationally running ≥6 months with at least one external contributor + at least one outside reviewer beyond the LAMPS-WG echo chamber. This preserves the option to publish later from a stronger evidentiary base without bearing the small-team-overreach risk now. Cost: ~6-12 month delay on public-stance signal; payoff: shipping evidence + at-least-one-other-pair-of-eyes derisks Position B materially.
downgrade_recommendation.minimum_acceptable_position: Position A with team-scale-caveat as the SECOND section after the lede. Anything weaker than this (e.g. publishing Position B with only minor wording softening) does not adequately mitigate the small-team-overreach risk.

load_bearing_findings: Team-capacity reality check: 1 human contributor / 0 stars / 0 forks / 0 releases / 5 weeks of public existence. Every claim about sustained engagement must be evaluated against this denominator.
Position B framing of F5 blog is the single largest reputational risk on the entire slate; downgrade to Position A with structural rewrite is mandatory if blog is to ship in this window.
F6 standalone library publication is a security-response trap; in-tree code linked from blog delivers identical inspectability without acquiring unsupportable downstream consumers.
F10 broad cross-system outreach has asymmetric leverage risk; iroh-only private email is the maximum acceptable scope; broader fan-out should be cut.
The plan's own Section 5 Failure Mode E ('if 4+ of 7 HIGH lenses return strongly-negative, downgrade to Position A') is the correct gate; this lens is voting that gate downward.

Plan correctly identifies the risks in Sections 5 + Shape-5 reflection; my objections are not 'plan missed this' but 'plan named these risks and then proceeded as if mitigation language alone is sufficient — for a one-human team, the structural risk persists regardless of mitigation prose.'
summary.overall_disposition: REQUEST DOWNGRADE — Position A with structural rewrite per downgrade_recommendation, F6 kept in-tree, F10 scoped to iroh-only private, F3/F4/F7 scoped to one-shot post-shipping. F2 unchanged. If Ben rejects the downgrade, the responsible alternative is DEFER blog publication until v1-beta has operational shipping evidence + at least one external reviewer outside the LAMPS-WG echo chamber.
what_would_change_my_verdict: If Benten gains 2+ additional active human maintainers AND a documented security-response process before publication, F5 Position B risk drops from VERY HIGH to MEDIUM and F6 standalone publication becomes defensible.

If v1-beta has been operationally running ≥6 months with externally-observable Atrium deployments, the 'pre-shipping blog' concern drops away and the position is anchored in evidence rather than promises.

If an outside reviewer (not Benten, not LAMPS WG, not the dispatched LLM lenses) reads the blog draft and signs off in writing, the small-team echo-chamber concern is materially reduced — though it does not eliminate the title/framing risks of Position B.

If iroh's private response (per the F10-iroh-only scoping above) is genuinely receptive — not polite-noncommittal — the coalition-shape from Shape-5 reflection becomes available and downgrades F5 risk substantially (moves Benten from 'alone' to 'first of two').
